subject: Capacity coordination: APAC node ask + EU reprioritization for two deals
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity coordination: APAC node ask + EU reprioritization for two deals

Team —

We have two parallel deals that need immediate capacity planning so ops/procurement can align timelines: Helix Labs (US-led, planning to expand to APAC) and MiraHealth (EU healthcare customer requiring strict region isolation). High level asks below; spreadsheet attached with initial forecasts.

Quick summary:
- Helix Labs (related_account: Helix Labs) wants APAC presence for their pilot: target start ~Aug 15, initial traffic forecast ~120 qps peak, 18M tokens/day estimated. They want reserved capacity for predictable latency.
- MiraHealth (related_account: MiraHealth) is EU-first, requires dedicated EU-only pool for PHI-like data, initial commit smaller but strict SLA and data residency.

Asks for this thread:
1) Karthik: rough sizing recommendation by region (preferred GPU type and count) + whether we can leverage a small APAC node (edge) rather than a full regional fleet for Helix.
2) Mina / Procurement: lead times and contract/PO constraints if we need to convert cloud credits to reserved capacity or pull from committed pool.
3) Ben: is there any existing burst or surplus we can tap in APAC or EU this quarter without impacting committed customers?

Attachment: capacity_request_20250718.xlsx (xlsx) — has forecast tabs for both deals and a simplified token/QPS model.

Goal: have a recommended plan (numbers + timeline + ownership) by end of day so I can confirm with the customers and lock a kickoff date.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity coordination: APAC node ask + EU reprioritization for two deals

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. High-level technical takeaways + rough sizing below. I pulled the forecast tab and assumed 50% concurrency on the QPS numbers with an average 1200-token context for Helix; MiraHealth is more bursty but lower sustained QPS.

Recommendations:
- APAC (Helix Labs pilot):
  - Start with a small dedicated APAC node: 4 x H100 (reserved) for sustained low-latency chat workloads. H100 gives headroom for larger context and quantization profiles we plan to recommend.
  - Configure autoscale/burst to +2 H100 (on-demand) to handle 20–30% traffic spikes.
  - Expected baseline throughput: ~75–120 qps depending on batching and prefix cache hit rates.
- EU (MiraHealth):
  - Because of data residency and strict isolation, provision 6 x A100s in a dedicated EU pool if the workloads are quantized 4-bit. If they require full fp16/large context models, move to 6 x H100.
  - If we reallocate from the existing EU pool temporarily, prioritize MiraHealth windows (their usage is weekday business hours).

Notes on tradeoffs:
- A100 vs H100: H100s reduce overall node counts for large-context models and improve latency for long sequences, but procurement/backfill costs are higher. For APAC pilot, H100 is preferable.
- Kernel selection and memory planning: we'll need the kernel_selection_notes.pdf (attached) to validate memory per-request; consider enabling KV prefix caching to reduce per-token compute.

Operational asks:
- Ben: verify current EU pool utilization and flag any committed customers that would be impacted by a 4-GPU reallocation.
- Mina: share standard contract language for short-term reallocation and any credits we can offer if we borrow against a committed pool.

I attached a quick technical note: kernel_selection_notes.pdf — it has microbenchmarks for H100 vs A100 on our current model catalog.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 12:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity coordination: APAC node ask + EU reprioritization for two deals

Jordan / team —

Procurement constraints and timing notes:
- Reserved capacity (cloud partner) can generally be turned on within 2–3 weeks once finance signs the PO and we have credit approvals; ordering physical or committed bare-metal fleets (customer-dedicated on-prem) can be 8–12+ weeks depending on vendor and custom networking.
- If we reallocate from an existing EU committed pool to MiraHealth, we need signoff from the current commitment owner and a formal SLA amendment. That process typically takes 5–7 business days for internal approvals.
- Suggested commercial options:
  1) Short-term borrow: temporary reallocation for 8 weeks, offering a 10% credit on monthly committed fees to the pool owner.
  2) Rapid reserved capacity via cloud partner: billable as reserved but with a 3-month minimum.
  3) Hybrid: start MiraHealth on cloud-reserved nodes while we formalize a dedicated pool.

Action items for procurement:
- Jordan: get target start date (you mentioned ~Aug 15) — confirm whether the customer needs full SLA day 1 or can accept a pilot with 99% latency SLO.
- Ben: please flag any contract owners that must approve temporary reallocation.

Attachment: procurement_timing.docx (docx) — includes lead-time matrix and standard amendment language.

-Minah
Head of Procurement, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Capacity coordination: APAC node ask + EU reprioritization for two deals

Jordan —

Thanks for looping us in. Quick clarifications from Helix side so we can lock timelines:
- Target pilot start: Aug 15 (agreed).
- Forecast: peak 120 qps, sustained 70 qps; concurrency ~0.6.
- Typical context: 1k–1.5k tokens; we plan to start on a trimmed model (quantized) but may switch to higher-capacity by month 2.

Can you confirm the proposed APAC node spec (4 x H100 + burst to 6 H100)? We are comfortable with that if we can get predictable latency and a documented rollback if performance isn't met. Also, any chance for a limited pilot discount?

Regards,
Sam Lee
Head of Platform Partnerships
Helix Labs

Team / Sam —

Thanks everyone for quick responses. Summarizing agreed next steps so we have one source of truth: 

Agreements:
- APAC node for Helix Labs: provision 4 x H100 reserved + burst policy to allow up to 2 additional H100s on-demand. Target go-live Aug 15; kickoff demo week of Aug 4. Owner: Karthik to validate perf profile and ops runbook; Jordan to confirm pilot SLOs and discount ask with Helix.
- EU for MiraHealth: we will temporarily reallocate up to 4 GPUs from the existing EU pool as a stopgap and enable a cloud-reserved option if procurement lead time pushes beyond 3 weeks. Owner: Mina to coordinate PO/amendment; Ben to confirm which pool nodes are safe to reassign.
- Commercials: Jordan to propose short-term credit (10%) for any pool owner impacted by temporary reallocation; Mina to draft amendment language and timeline.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Karthik: finalize kernel selection + H100 vs A100 perf tab (ETA: Jul 22). (attachment: kernel_selection_notes.pdf)
- Mina: procurement lead-time matrix + amendment draft (ETA: Jul 25). (attachment: procurement_timing.docx)
- Ben: EU pool impact report (ETA: Jul 21).
- Jordan: confirm Helix discount ask and send signed pilot SOW to Sam (ETA: Jul 20).

Links: HubSpot deal HL-3421 (https://hubspot.example.com/deal/HL-3421) and DocuSign for pilot SOW (https://app.redwood.com/contract/DOCU-SIGN-FF12-8B).

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the kickoff demo (proposed Aug 4).

Thanks — Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
